Subject: Request: topology & SIG evidence for Dedicated/Private deployment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OmniCloud is moving forward with a pilot of Redwood Dedicated for a regulated workload. Our security team has asked for a focused packet to to complete the SIG questionnaire and our internal risk review. Specifically they want:

- A network-level topology diagram that highlights tenant segregation boundaries for both Dedicated and Private deployments.
- A short narrative explaining how control plane traffic is separated from inference/data plane and what egress controls exist for KV/cache and model payloads.
- A checklist of artifacts we can hand to our auditors (diagram, firewall rules summary, attestation).

Can you share an annotated topology (PDF) and a SIG evidence checklist? We need the packet by end of next week (Mar 26).

Thanks,

Priya Rao

priya@omnicloud.com

Hi Priya — appreciate the clear ask. Attaching an annotated topology and a SIG-targeted checklist. Highlights below and next steps: 

Attachments included in this email: redwood-dedicated-topology-v1.pdf, segregation-evidence-checklist-SIG.xlsx, network-annotations_v2.png

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Dedicated: customer gets a reserved GPU pool and logical tenant overlay; control plane (orchestrator) runs in a separate management VPC with one-way-authenticated control channels into inference nodes. Tenants are isolated via per-tenant namespaces + strict network policies and per-tenant egress ACLs.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): control plane optionally runs in customer VPC or local airgapped control plane; when control plane is customer-hosted, Redwood operators do not have direct data plane access.
- KV/cache egress: KV cache is tenancy-scoped and defaults to no external egress. Where we allow cache replication (rare), it runs over mTLS channels to specified endpoints and is logged.

Roadmap to deliverables:
1) You have the PDF & PNG attached now (these are high-level annotated diagrams).
2) We will produce a short narrative and a SOC2/SIG evidence bundle (firewall rules snippets, example audit log export) by Mar 24.
3) Karthik and Evelyn are looped to validate the SOC/SIG artifacts and add any network ACL snippets.

If this covers it, I can produce a one-page attestation for your auditors. Any specific SIG domains you want prioritized (e.g., network zoning, key management, egress)?

Best,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales (Security & Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — quick technical notes to include in the narrative and evidence pack: 

1) Control plane separation: the control plane uses a dedicated management subnet with no inbound Internet routes; orchestration API endpoints are reachable only from operator jump hosts and customer-managed bastions. Add a diagram inset showing the management subnet route table.

2) Data-plane KV/cache egress: default policy denies all external addresses. When customers enable cross-region replication we require an explicit allow-list and HMAC-based signing of replication payloads; include the kvcache replication policy snippet (attached).

3) TLS & mTLS: all east-west traffic between nodes uses mTLS with certs rotated via our KMS-backed CA. The checklist should reference key rotation cadence and audit log retention (we keep rotation events and CA actions for 2 years in the control plane audit).

4) Firewall rule example: provide a sample iptables/fw rule for tenant egress limitations; I added a one-line example in the appendix.

I'll attach the appendix (segregation-appendix-kvcache-egress.txt) with snippets you can include verbatim in the SIG evidence workbook.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference
